description: Sync opportunities, candidates, job postings, contacts, submitted applications and referral forms from Lever. Opportunities link to their contact, and applications link to their candidate when Lever supplies the candidate id.
opening: Sync opportunities, candidates, job postings, contacts, submitted applications and referral forms from one Lever account. Each record is one document. An opportunity links to its contact, and an application links to its candidate when Lever supplies the candidate id. Referral forms are not linked to a candidate.

Lever permissions are not imported, so every synced record is visible to everyone who can query the collection unless you set an access rule. Selecting postings limits only postings: everything else syncs for the whole account. Edits to an application or referral form after it is first synced are not guaranteed to be picked up. Archived records stay in HydraDB, and deleted ones can stay.

notes: An access rule on a posting does not cover opportunities, candidates, contacts, applications or referral forms, which sync for the whole account.

steps.title: Get an API key
steps.text: Get a Lever API key for your account.

steps.title: Select postings
steps.text: HydraDB lists your job postings. Select the postings to sync. This selection limits postings only. Opportunities, candidates, contacts, applications and referral forms sync for the whole account whatever you select.

connect.account: One connector reads one Lever account.

sync.first_sync: Reaches back the window set by `lookback_days`, 30 days by default.
sync.changes: Opportunities, candidates and selected postings are picked up when they are updated. Contacts, applications and referral forms are reached only through the candidates read in the same sync. A contact is read when such a candidate refers to it. An application or referral form is read when it was created within the sync window.
sync.edits: An updated opportunity, candidate or posting replaces its document. A contact is read again only when a candidate that refers to it is read. Edits to an application or referral form after it is first synced are not guaranteed to be picked up.
sync.deletes: Records deleted in Lever can stay searchable in HydraDB. Archiving a candidate or application in Lever does not remove or hide its document.
notes: An opportunity and a candidate that share an id share one document, so the one read last is the one you see.

shared_attributes.name: connector_id
shared_attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's records. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: Lever id
shared_attributes.text: The record's Lever id, written into the text as its key. Searchable on every record type except contacts.

documents.name: Opportunities
documents.one_document: One opportunity. A candidate with the same id shares this document.
documents.title: The person's name. Otherwise `Lever opportunity` and its id.
documents.text: The name, then `Headline`, `Stage`, `Origin`, `Tags` and `Emails` lines. The creation time is part of the text. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: When the opportunity was last updated, or created when there is no update time.
documents.files: Resumes and other files are not synced.

attributes.name: name, headline
attributes.text: The person's name and profile headline. The name forms the title.

attributes.name: Stage
attributes.text: The stage's display name. When the name cannot be found, the stage id is written instead.

attributes.name: origin, tags, emails
attributes.text: Whether the person applied, was sourced or was referred, their tags and their email addresses.

attributes.name: contact
attributes.text: Links the opportunity to its Lever contact. Not searchable.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the opportunity was created. It is the result date only when there is no update time.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.text: When the opportunity was last updated. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.lever_opportunity_id
attributes.text: The Lever opportunity id. Finds one opportunity. Not searchable.

attributes.name: owner
attributes.text: The owner's Lever user id. It is not turned into a name.

documents.name: Candidates
documents.one_document: One candidate. Lever's candidate and opportunity views of the same record share one document.
documents.title: The candidate's name. Otherwise `Lever candidate` and its id.
documents.text: The name, then `Headline`, `Location`, `Stage`, `Origin`, `Tags`, `Emails` and `Links` lines. The creation time is part of the text. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: When the candidate was last interacted with, or created when there is no interaction time.
documents.files: Resumes and other files are not synced.

attributes.name: name, headline, location
attributes.text: The candidate's name, profile headline and location. The name forms the title.

attributes.name: Stage
attributes.text: The stage's display name. When the name cannot be found, the stage id is written instead.

attributes.name: origin, tags, emails
attributes.text: Whether the candidate applied, was sourced or was referred, their tags and their email addresses.

attributes.name: links
attributes.text: The candidate's profile links on other sites. They are not links back to Lever.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the candidate was created. It is the result date only when there is no interaction time.

attributes.name: last_interaction_at
attributes.text: When the candidate was last interacted with. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.lever_candidate_id
attributes.text: The Lever candidate id. Finds one candidate. Not searchable.

attributes.name: archived
attributes.text: Whether Lever marks the candidate as archived. It does not remove or hide the document.

documents.name: Postings
documents.title: The posting title. Otherwise `Lever posting` and its id.
documents.text: The title, then `Team`, `Department`, `Location` and `Commitment` lines and the posting description as plain text. The creation time is part of the text. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: When the posting was last updated, or created when there is no update time.
documents.link_back: The posting's public page, or its listing page when there is none.

attributes.name: categories
attributes.text: The posting's team, department, location and commitment. Other category values are stored but not searchable.

attributes.name: Description
attributes.text: The posting description. Lists and additional sections of the posting are not kept.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the posting was created. It is the result date only when there is no update time.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.text: When the posting was last updated. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.lever_posting_id
attributes.text: The Lever posting id. Finds one posting. Not searchable.

attributes.name: owner, user
attributes.text: The Lever user ids of the posting's owner and creator. They are not turned into names.

documents.name: Contacts
documents.one_document: One contact person that a synced candidate refers to.
documents.title: The contact's name. Otherwise `Lever contact` and its id.
documents.text: `Name`, `Headline`, `Location`, `Emails`, `Phones`, `Links` and `Tags` lines. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: When the contact was last updated, or created when there is no update time.

attributes.name: name, headline, location
attributes.text: The contact's name, headline and location. The name forms the title.

attributes.name: emails, phones
attributes.text: The contact's email addresses and phone numbers, in the text only. They do not make the contact a person in the graph.

attributes.name: links, tags
attributes.text: The contact's profile links and tags.

attributes.name: updated_at, created_at
attributes.text: When the contact was last updated, or created. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.lever_contact_id
attributes.text: The Lever contact id. Finds one contact. Not searchable.

documents.name: Applications
documents.title: `Application from` and the applicant's name. Otherwise `Lever application`.
documents.text: `Type`, `Name`, `Email`, `Company`, `Phone` and `Comments` lines, then each custom question with its answer. The creation time is part of the text. The title is searchable too.

attributes.name: Applicant details
attributes.text: The applicant's name, email, company and phone as given on the application. They are in the text only, not kept as separate fields.

attributes.name: type, comments
attributes.text: How the application came in, and the applicant's comments.

attributes.name: Answers
attributes.text: Each custom question with a non-empty answer, in the text only.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.lever_candidate_id
attributes.text: The candidate id, when Lever supplies it. Limits a query to one candidate's applications, and links the application to the candidate. Not searchable.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the application was created. It is the result date.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.lever_application_id
attributes.text: The Lever application id. Finds one application. Not searchable.

attributes.name: posting
attributes.text: The id of the posting applied to. It does not link the application to the posting, and it is not a query filter.

attributes.name: archived
attributes.text: Lever's archive details for the application. They do not remove or hide the document.

documents.name: Referral forms
documents.title: The form title. Otherwise `Lever referral` and its id.
documents.text: `Type`, `Stage` and `Instructions` lines, then each question with its answer. The candidate's name is not added. The creation time is part of the text. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: When the form was completed, or created when there is no completion time.

attributes.name: type, instructions
attributes.text: The form type and its instructions.

attributes.name: Stage
attributes.text: The stage's display name. When the name cannot be found, the stage id is written instead.

attributes.name: Answers
attributes.text: Each question with a non-empty answer.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the form was created. It is the result date only when there is no completion time.

attributes.name: completed_at
attributes.text: When the form was completed. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.lever_referral_id
attributes.text: The Lever referral id. Finds one referral form. Not searchable.

attributes.name: user, referrer
attributes.text: The Lever user ids of the person who completed the form and the referrer. They are not turned into names, and the referrer is not linked.

example_searches: Which candidates mention the onsite stage?
What comments and answers are recorded in this application?
Which postings mention the Engineering department?

connections: An application to its candidate, when Lever supplies the candidate id.
Applications are not linked to their posting, and referral forms are not linked to a candidate.
graph.people: No one is attached to a record as a person. Owners, creators and referrers are kept as Lever user ids only. Candidate and contact names are in the text.
graph.from_text: Profiles, posting descriptions, application comments and answers, and referral form answers.

not_synced: Lever users, requisitions, sources and tags as documents.
Whether a posting is open or closed, and posting sections other than its categories and description.
Separate fields for contact phone numbers, applicant profile details and question answers. Their values are in the text only.
Deletions: records deleted in Lever can stay in HydraDB.
